title: Reconstruction Dynamics Consolidation Review
purpose: Review MPF-RDYN-001 through MPF-RDYN-009 as a coherent bounded reconstruction-dynamics scaffold and determine whether dynamics exploration remains safe for continued analog-only investigation.
review_findings: Reconstruction flows successfully quantify accessibility evolution without final closure claims.
Stabilization basins define local persistence without implying physical equilibrium.
Deformation propagation classes effectively track distortion spread and risk.
Recursive coupling is rigorously governed to prevent closure or feedback-identity overclaims.
Embedded observer dynamic constraints define mandatory gaps in reconstruction flows.
Drift detection provides a linguistic firewall against dynamics-language escalation.
Stress tests confirm robustness against injected convergence absolutism and closure assumptions.
remaining_risks: Stabilization basins may be psychologically misread as universal attractors.
Recursive feedback complexity requires continuous loss-accounting monitoring.
Observer participation complicates the extraction of 'stable' dynamic metrics.
forbidden_next_steps: Claiming recursive coupling proves ontology identity.
